question: How much of the raw long-range field-goal make rate is who kicks and in what conditions, and what does an average kicker make?
post_hoc: Post hoc: this model, the support distance and the cap or override it offers the planner were designed after seeing the world-model run on branch claude/world-model-colab (results/world_model/colab_t4_v2), whose simulated long-range make rate was above the raw training rate. They are not part of that run's preregistered plan.

decomposition.method: Shapley split of model_fit - selection_free over four factors (kicker, conditions, heave, era); 90% intervals from 1,000 draws of the Gaussian approximation at the mode (Sigma held fixed).

support.rule: The support distance is the largest integer distance D such that every distance d from 40 to D satisfies both: (a) top-decile kickers (top 10% by estimated 50-yard strength among kickers with at least 100 training attempts) made at least 20 training attempts with distance in [d - 2, d + 2]; and (b) the median over those kickers of the width of the 90% interval of their own predicted make rate at d (neutral conditions, 2021) is at most 0.2.

calibration_check.note: Season trend extrapolated from 2021. Weather missing outdoors is filled with the training median. Kickers not seen in training get the average kicker.

synthetic_selection_world.description: 80 kickers, 150 attempts each, strength u ~ Normal(0, 0.5) in log-odds, attempt distance Normal(38 + 12 u, 9): strong kickers kick longer. Rates on attempts of 55 yards or more (kicker.simulate_selected_attempts).
